title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, reconstructed from pp. 78-80. M is a 'structure': a set of objects X (regions or 'pieces') with a symmetric disjointness relation X ∥ Y.

For A ⊂ M:
- compl A = {Y : Y ∥ X for all X ∈ A} is the orthogonal (polar) complement.
- supp A = compl(compl A) is the bi-orthogonal closure, the 'support'.
- Σ_M is the set of saturated subsets (A = supp A). It is a complete lattice with an involution C = compl, i.e. the ortholattice of closed sets of a Birkhoff polarity.

A 'realization' is a map X ↦ |X| into 𝔓(P) for a set P, with X ∥ Y ⇔ |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅ (Supp¹), extended by |A| = ∪_{X∈A} |X|.

On p. 78 (Lemma 2), assuming |compl A| = P∖|A|, Grothendieck showed:
- |A| = |supp A|;
- supp A ⊂ supp B ⇔ |A| ⊂ |B|;
- Σ_M → 𝔓(P) is an order embedding commuting with the involutions C_M and C_P.

This page asks whether this embedding also respects Sup and Inf. By complementation it suffices to treat Inf. In Σ_M the Inf of a family of saturated A_i is their intersection. One always has (X): |∧A_i| = |∩A_i| ⊂ ∩|A_i|, and the question is equality. A crossed-out attempt via the complement U = |∨A_i| fails.

He then introduces a much stronger hypothesis, 'Hyp!' (later called Supp²): every point x ∈ P is realized exactly, i.e. there is X ∈ M with |X| = {x}. This hypothesis:
- implies surjectivity of Σ_M → 𝔓(P);
- implies the complement formula |compl A| = P∖|A|. If x ∉ |A|, its singleton-object X is disjoint from every |Z| with Z ∈ A, so X ∥ A by Supp¹, hence X ∈ compl A.
- gives equality in (X). If x ∈ ∩|A_i|, pick X with |X| = {x}. Then |X| ⊂ |A_i| ⇒ supp X ⊂ supp A_i = A_i ⇒ X ∈ A_i for all i ⇒ X ∈ ∩A_i ⇒ x ∈ |∩A_i| (finished on p. 80).

The outcome (Proposition, p. 80) is that under Supp¹ and Supp², Σ_M ≅ 𝔓(P) as complete ortholattices. In other words, an orthogonality space whose objects include 'point-objects' detecting disjointness has the Boolean algebra 𝔓(P) as its lattice of bi-orthogonally closed sets. This serves Grothendieck's axiomatic 'analysis situs': recovering a point-set picture from a calculus of pieces and their disjointness.
errors: No mathematical error. The crossed-out complement argument is abandoned, not wrong.

The proof sketch silently uses that |X| ⊂ |A_i| implies supp X ⊂ supp A_i; this is exactly Lemma 2, which Supp² supplies via the complement formula. So the argument is complete only once that implication is noted, which he does.
Minor: the transcription writes '∀A ∈ M' in the complement formula; it must be ∀A ⊂ M.

ideas.what: Lattice of bi-orthogonally closed subsets of a set with a disjointness relation, with complement involution (supp = compl∘compl)
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity; orthogonality space (Dacey, Foulis-Randall); complete ortholattice of closed sets
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the published parts of the Analysis situs chapter; otherwise unsure

ideas.what: Realization of pieces by subsets of a point set, with every point exactly realized, making the closed-set lattice isomorphic to 𝔓(P) and preserving arbitrary Inf/Sup
ideas.modern_name: Atomistic orthospace / atomic Boolean representation; point-free versus pointed mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Stone-type representation, mereotopology: Whitehead, de Laguna, Tarski)

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary and correct lemma in an axiomatic set-up of 'pieces' and disjointness. It is standard polarity/orthogonality-space reasoning; nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'Est indiquée déjà la surjectivité' is more likely 'Elle implique déjà la surjectivité (vi_M bis)'.
'articulations C' is probably 'involutions C' (cf. p. 78: 'commute à involution C_M, C_P').
The formula reads '|co-supp A| = P∖|A| ∀A ⊂ M' (subsets, not elements).
'(les A_i des parties ouvertes [?])' is likely 'des parties saturées' (elements of Σ_M), given that the Inf is the intersection.
